sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 1113.2 ± 193.6 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

literature_notes: Two ledger lines were evaluated. L1 describes an 'HA signal peptide' added to the N-terminus of BRS3 for expression of BRS3–Gq complexes. This is the hemagglutinin signal sequence used to route the receptor through the secretory pathway — it is a cleavable signal peptide, not the HA epitope tag (YPYDVPDYA). Per the instructions, a tag placed upstream of the mature protein is 'cleaved off with the SP — a silent failure'; it would not be present on the cell surface. L1 therefore does not report a surface epitope-tag insertion and does not qualify. L2 describes a C-terminal fusion of BRS3 to LgBiT (NanoBiT tethering strategy). The BRS3 C-terminus (residue 399) falls within the intracellular span 331–399; this is an intracellular fusion, not a surface tag. It is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports a surface-displayed epitope-tag insertion at any extracellular site of BRS3.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal LgBiT fusion used for NanoBiT tethering in structural studies; residue 399 lies within the intracellular C-terminal tail (topology 331–399), so this is an intracellular fusion, not a surface tag.
